articles.title: BBC News app
articles.description: Top stories, breaking news, live reporting, and follow news topics that match your interests

articles.title: UK growth upgraded but energy prices and rates to bite in 2027
articles.description: The IMF report comes as final preparations are being made to the first Budget under Prime Minister Andy Burham.

articles.title: Why the prime minister wants to talk about Brexit again
articles.description: For the first time since the UK left the EU, we have a prime minister who will "unflinchingly" debate Brexit, says the BBC's political editor Chris Mason.

articles.title: Saudi minister vows 'serious response' to Houthi attacks on airports
articles.description: It comes after the armed group hit Riyadh's international airport and another facility, killing 13 people, in a significant escalation.

articles.title: Hundreds more prisoners to be freed in second phase of early release scheme
articles.description: Second tranche of prisoners will include those serving up to two and a half years for crimes.

articles.title: The Papers: 'Burnham ready to sign new EU deal' and 'Hand of Gord'
articles.description: Many of today's papers cover the PM's comments on Brexit and the Daily Star writes of an alleged exorcism.

articles.title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure
articles.description: The settlement follows the largest group legal action brought by midwives in the UK, says union.

articles.title: I lost my hair to MS treatment - now my wigs are worn by Naomi Campbell and Serena Williams
articles.description: Antonia Okonma Shittu's wig business was launched after a shock diagnosis, and she now wants to help other women feel their best.

articles.title: Breaking Bad actor RJ Mitte dies aged 34
articles.description: Mitte, who lived with cerebral palsy, starred as Walter White Jr in the Emmy-winning drama series.

articles.title: Pope Leo Will Have Surgery to Remove Growth on Lung
articles.description: A recent medical examination found a small nodule, he announced, adding that doctors would remove it this week.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Has Few Options as Houthis Aim at Heart of Its Ambitions
articles.description: Three deadly attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen on an airport in the Saudi capital underscored the asymmetrical nature of their conflict with the kingdom.

articles.title: Over 100 Migrants Are Dead After Boat Capsizes Near Djibouti
articles.description: The shipwreck is among the deadliest ever recorded on the route to Yemen, the International Organization for Migration said. Dozens remain missing, and the bodies of 15 children were recovered.

articles.title: Ukraine Shrugs Off Trump Call to Ditch Zelensky for Energy Strikes
articles.description: President Trump lashed out at President Volodymyr Zelensky for striking Russian oil refineries. Mr. Zelensky said he’ll stop — if Russia does too.

articles.title: Pakistan Seizes Control of an Opposition-Led Province
articles.description: The federal government, speaking of “a severe breakdown in law and order” in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid militant violence, named a politically allied official as in charge.

articles.title: India’s ‘Cockroach’ Leaders Released as Small Protests Go On in Delhi
articles.description: The leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party, an Indian youth movement, had been detained by the police on Saturday before they could lead protests over voting rights.

articles.title: Man Dies in Tiger Attack at Yorkshire Wildlife Park in England
articles.description: The man came face to face with an Amur tiger inside the animal’s habitat at Yorkshire Wildlife Park in England. The park was evacuated and closed to the public.

articles.title: Wringing Hope From the Rubble of Gaza
articles.description: The cease-fire last October ostensibly brought an end to Israel’s war in Gaza after the Hamas-led attacks on Oct. 7, 2023. A year later, however, Israeli strikes, though less frequent, haven’t stopped.

articles.title: What to Know About the Protests in India
articles.description: Scattered protests against sweeping revisions to India’s voter rolls broke out on Sunday in New Delhi. The police met earlier protests with an extraordinary show of force.

articles.title: A Russian Spy’s Lone Regret: ‘I Got Caught’
articles.description: Though born in Ukraine, Alexsander supports the Russian cause. He wishes he had deleted one photo from his phone.

articles.title: A Reporter Returns to China to Find it Richer, but Also Highly Paranoid.
articles.description: Returning to China after decades away, a correspondent finds bullet trains, dazzling skylines — and a surveillance state more paranoid and pervasive than ever.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh Airport Attacked Again, After Days of Houthi Strikes
articles.description: The strike on Saturday was the deadliest attack in a Gulf Arab country since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began in February, and forced the airport to temporarily suspend operations.

articles.title: Rebuking Ukraine Over Oil Strikes, Trump Says It Should ‘Get a New President’
articles.description: Hours after President Trump said the United States would buy Russian diesel, the Kremlin said there would be no immediate resumption of discussions to end the war.

articles.title: Quebec Independence Is Unlikely, but Some Will Still Dream
articles.description: The idea of independence remains deeply unpopular in Quebec, yet the separatist Parti Québécois was re-elected to a minority government this week.

articles.title: 3 Men Found Guilty in Murders of Tourists on Mexico Surf Trip
articles.description: The 2024 killings of two Australian brothers and their American friend drew international attention.

articles.title: A Week Later, Russia Hasn’t Said What Pathogen Killed Plague Researcher
articles.description: Experts said they believed that with modern testing technology, the Russian authorities should know the answer by now.

articles.title: Palestinian Authority Formally Delays Elections, Despite Western Pressure
articles.description: The aging Palestinian leader, Mahmoud Abbas, pushed off the planned vote until late 2027. Palestinians haven’t had major elections for about two decades.

articles.title: Indian Police Round Up Protest Leaders and Lock Down Delhi
articles.description: Thousands of young people tried to gather to protest a sweeping revision of their country’s voter roll. Security forces hauled many of them away.

articles.title: From a Sikh Sanctuary to Chaotic Streets, Protesters Brave Police in Delhi
articles.description: A group of demonstrators used a house of worship known as a gurdwara as a staging ground before their long-shot effort to reach a locked-down protest site in New Delhi.

articles.title: Inside Erik Prince’s Mercenary Deal in Congo
articles.description: The injury of a former Green Beret and death of an elite soldier from New Zealand have highlighted the Blackwater founder’s growing role in one of Africa’s most intractable conflicts.

articles.title: Navi Pillay, Nobel Peace Prize Winner, Forged Her Career Under Apartheid
articles.description: Navi Pillay, who won this year’s Nobel Peace Prize, fought racism in South Africa, shaping her international career as a judge and advocate for justice and human rights.

articles.title: Blocked by Police, India’s Youth Voice Their Fury
articles.description: Members of a youth protest movement are outraged after being intercepted at airports and stopped by barricades. “Aren’t we children of this nation?”

articles.title: 7.7-Magnitude Panama Earthquake Sets Off Series of Aftershocks
articles.description: The quake, which had a preliminary magnitude of 7.7, was centered in the country’s southern region.

articles.title: Publicly owned rail is popular. But is it making the trains run on time?
articles.description: Meeting travellers' expectations could be challenging, experts warn.

articles.title: US actress Selma Blair accused of assault after incident with flight attendants
articles.description: The Legally Blonde star is investigated by the FBI following an alleged altercation on a flight from LA to New York.

articles.title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise
articles.description: Heating oil customers facing soaring bills are promised better regulation of the sector by the government.

articles.title: I earn £120,000 a year making social media videos go viral
articles.description: Social media "clippers" make short, vertical videos that appear on the likes of Instagram and TikTok.

articles.title: Coventry announce themselves back in the big time
articles.description: Coventry climb out of the relegation zone after ending their 25-year wait for a top-flight goal and victory in front of their own fans.

articles.title: Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?
articles.description: After every round of Premier League matches this season, Troy Deeney gives us his team of the week. Do you agree with his choices?

articles.title: After Russian Diesel Deal, Trump Faces New Crisis Over Ukraine
articles.description: President Trump’s surprise decision to suspend sanctions on Russian diesel fuel stunned Ukrainian and European officials, who were meeting with U.S. envoys at an exclusive golf club near Miami.

articles.title: Immigration agents search Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar's home
articles.description: Omar, an outspoken Trump critic, said the search was "an attempt to target political enemies" and she "will not be silenced".

articles.title: Dozens Killed in Airstrikes Near Sudan-Egypt Border
articles.description: The attacks occurred at a remote gold mine hundreds of miles from the front lines of Sudan’s devastating civil war. Videos showed what appeared to be Egyptian munitions.

articles.title: Coventry thrash Newcastle to claim first home win of season
articles.description: Coventry City stun Newcastle United with an emphatic 4-1 victory as they win their first Premier League game at home in 25 years.

articles.title: Six Ukrainian energy sites hit by Russia since Trump announced ceasefire, Zelensky says
articles.description: Despite the US president announcing energy infrastructure would not be targeted strikes have continued, Ukraine says.

articles.title: Jordan 'Last Dance' jersey sells for record £10.6m
articles.description: A Michael Jordan jersey from his 'Last Dance' season sells for $14m (£10.6m), a record for a piece of basketball memorabilia.

articles.title: Qantas flight grounded after bedbug outbreak
articles.description: The flight from Italy to Australia was cancelled after passengers on the plane's previous journey complained of bug bites.

articles.title: NATO Details Plan to Shield Ukraine’s European Allies From Russia
articles.description: With the Russians intensifying sabotage, arson and cyberattacks against European nations supporting Ukraine, NATO divulged a blueprint, in case of war, to deter the Kremlin.

articles.title: Cornell and Toxic Frat Culture
articles.description: A U.S. campus lawsuit points to a global pattern: how male impunity, silence and institutional failure enable sexual violence.

articles.title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs
articles.description: Shabana Mahmood says there is "insufficient protection" for those who play a role in public life.

articles.title: Britain won't tolerate threats on our soil, Miliband says as he summons Iran ambassador
articles.description: The prime minister says Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard "almost certainly" directed the RAF Fairford incident.

articles.title: Saracens sack academy player Auvaa after latest incident
articles.description: Saracens sack Totoa Auvaa, the academy player who was involved in a nightclub incident with England cricketers Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson, after another incident.
